schema: Reviewer judgments keyed by test id (file::name). `judgment` is one of STRONG (the assertions establish the claim and would fail if the behaviour broke), ADEQUATE (establishes the claim with a known limit), WEAK (could pass with a broken implementation, or checks less than it claims), STRUCTURAL (a rule about the code's shape, not behaviour; legitimate but exercises no project function). `why` says what was read. Reviewed on main at bc9d155 (2026-11-01).

tests/test_scoring_integrity.py::test_sc.why: Compares a scored simulator with an unscored twin on state, clock, event count and the next thirty ticks of readings, so any RNG draw or state write by `evaluate` would show.

tests/test_scoring_integrity.py::test_th.why: Equality of whole Score models across a repeat and a twin.

tests/test_scoring_integrity.py::test_a_.why: Four truth-side marks checked before and after 300 more ticks for every one-fault case.

tests/test_observation_tools.py::test_no.why: Calls every tool after 1200 ticks with a fault present, requires non-empty answers, checks hidden words are absent and pins the exact key set of every answer, so a new field cannot appear unnoticed. Limit: a leak carried inside a message string in other words would not be caught.

tests/test_episode.py::test_the_agent_ne.why: Searches the final working memory for four hidden words. It would miss a leak that carries the truth under another name (a machine id alone is not hidden, so it cannot be used); the key-set test in test_observation_tools is the stronger guard.

tests/test_known_answers.py::test_no_rec.why: Checks every state the stand-in saw for two words; the same limit as above. The pinned-anomaly test and the key-set test carry most of the weight.

tests/test_known_answers.py::test_scores.why: Pins relevant evidence collected, resolved, recommendation_correct and actions_taken for all thirteen cases with a look-once stand-in; a change in scoring or in a case's factory fails it.

tests/test_known_answers.py::test_the_su.why: Whole-record equality across two runs, excluding only wall time.

tests/test_agent_verification.py::test_n.why: Runs the check with a provider that would expose truth-like fields and asserts the judgement rests on the policy's cited observable evidence only.

tests/test_agent_verification.py::test_a.why: Parametrized windows that start at or before the work finish are shown to give inconclusive.

tests/test_agent_investigation.py::test_.why: Documents the limit of `check_conclusion` honestly: mechanically valid citations pass whatever they say. This is the test that proves the evaluator needs an evidence-quality judge.

tests/test_agent_loop.py::test_confidenc.why: A 0.95 hypothesis with one supporter does not stop the test phase; a second observable supporter does.

tests/test_model_policy.py::test_a_whole.why: Scripted JSON replies drive a full episode: proves the prompt/answer plumbing and the stage sequence, not reasoning quality. Must not be read as evidence that the agent diagnoses well.

tests/test_model_policy.py::test_no_prom.why: Guards the 'find the cause in the evidence' rule against prompt edits; string-based but exact.

tests/test_critic.py::test_system_prompt.why: A text rule on the prompt; exercises no project function but protects the hidden-truth boundary in prose.

tests/test_critic.py::test_review_does_n.why: Model-dump equality before and after review.

tests/test_evaluation.py::test_a_reset_r.why: Asserts only `action_correct and score.resolved` (truthiness). It does not check what the action list holds or that resolution comes from `speed_setting` being None rather than, say, the batch rule; a broken `_resolved` that returned True for any setting case would pass.

tests/test_evaluation.py::test_rejected_.why: Truthiness-only assertions on three fields; the rejected proposal's status text and the empty actions list are not checked explicitly.

tests/test_evaluation.py::test_no_answer.why: Negated truthiness on the two root-cause marks is what the claim needs, but the recommendation side is untested here.

tests/test_experiment.py::test_results_f.why: Backward-compatibility of the record format; exercises only pydantic parsing.

tests/test_agent_artifacts.py::test_the_.why: An import-graph rule enforced by reading source; exercises no project function but is the architectural guard the AGENTS.md boundary needs.

tests/test_console.py::test_without_it_t.why: Flagged as having no assertion because it relies on pytest.raises context; it does check the failure path it claims.

tests/test_bearing_degradation.py::test_.why: Truthiness on an equality of reading lists is enough for the claim; flagged by the heuristic only because the comparison is written as one boolean expression.

tests/test_baseline.py::test_the_right_r.why: Truthiness-only on action_correct/resolved; does not pin which repair or that nothing was proposed on the false alarm beyond a falsy check.

tests/test_evals.py::test_full_episode_r.why: Checks the policy saw no truth words and that accuracy is None without a label and set only with one.

tests/test_evals.py::test_comparison_req.why: Proves what `compare_reports` refuses; it cannot prove what it should refuse but does not (configuration differences).

tests/test_hazards.py::test_an_episode_w.why: Whole-record equality across two hazard runs plus the fired list.

tests/test_manual.py::test_no_section_gi.why: Guards numeric leaks of standard speeds and job times into the manual.
